message.content:
Painting the Eiffel Tower is a massive undertaking that involves a lot of logistics, safety work, and sheer volume of material.  In practice, the tower is repainted every seven years, and the whole job normally takes **about two months**.

Here’s why:

| Factor | Details |
|--------|---------|
| **Height** | 324 m (1,063 ft) |
| **Surface area** | Roughly 10 000 m² (≈ 107 000 ft²) |
| **Paint required** | ~60 tons of paint (about 1 ton per 170 m²) |
| **Crew size** | 30–40 workers (including climbers, painters, safety crews, and logistics staff) |
| **Work schedule** | 8‑hour days, 5 days a week (weather permitting) |
| **Safety & logistics** | 3‑4 weeks of preparation (rigging, scaffolding, permits, traffic control) |
| **Actual painting** | 4–6 weeks of continuous work on the tower’s exterior |

So, if you’re planning a hypothetical paint job, you’d expect roughly **8–10 weeks** of active painting, plus a few weeks of prep and cleanup, which brings the total to about **two months**.
